{"m": "gpt-4o", "msg": [{"content": "You compare short personal anecdotes by their underlying relational structure - the pattern of intentions, causes, deceptions, reversals, and outcomes among the people involved - NOT by their surface topic, setting, or vocabulary. Two stories can be about totally different situations yet share the same deep structure; two stories can share the same topic yet have opposite structure.", "role": "system"}, {"content": "SITUATION:
I despised my assigned lab partner—she was arrogant and dismissive. We were stuck together for a year-long research project. During a 36-hour experiment that went wrong, we problem-solved through the night, discovered we had the same dark humor, and became genuine collaborators. She's now my co-founder.

CANDIDATE A:
My upstairs neighbor and I had been in a noise complaint war for months. Then the building flooded and we both lost hot water for a week. Sharing kettle-boiled water and space heaters, we discovered we'd both recently divorced and loved obscure jazz. Now we have dinner together weekly.

CANDIDATE B:
I despised my assigned lab partner from day one—she was arrogant and dismissive. A year of forced collaboration didn't change anything. We completed the project professionally but never connected. Some antagonism doesn't resolve into friendship.

Which candidate shares the same underlying relational structure as the SITUATION (ignore surface topic similarity)? Respond as JSON: {"choice": "A" or "B", "reason": "<one sentence>"}.", "role": "user"}], "t": 0.0, "tag": "exp2:35"}
content: {"choice": "A", "reason": "Both stories involve initial animosity that transforms into a positive relationship through shared adversity and discovery of common interests."}
